metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened gate.jpeg in GIMP (2850x5070 RGB), navigated Image > Mode and Image > Color Management submenus, then pressed Escape.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Image menu including Scale Image option. Demonstrated ability to interact with GIMP transform/mode menus.
metadata.explanation: The original image is 2850x5070 pixels. This task asks to scale to exactly half (1425x2535). Evaluator reads the overwritten gate.jpeg via PIL and checks dimensions match expected ±5px tolerance. Initial state (2850x5070) fails the check, ensuring negative-control resistance.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads gate.jpeg from /home/user/Desktop/gate.jpeg using PIL and returns width/height — directly checks the overwritten file on disk.
Metric correctly compares actual dimensions to expected 1425x2535 with ±5px tolerance, awarding 0.5 per correct dimension (1.0 total if both match).
Expected values (1425, 2535) match the instruction exactly.
Negative-control resistance is ensured: initial state (2850x5070) will fail both dimension checks.
Getter handles file-not-found and PIL read errors gracefully, returning 0.0 in those cases.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: The postconfig uses ctrl+shift+e (Export As) + Enter to force-export before checking. If the agent scaled but did not save, postconfig will auto-save for it, effectively bypassing the 'overwrite the file' requirement. Consider verifying the file modification timestamp or using a script that only exports if GIMP has unsaved changes.

JPEG dimensions are lossless and do not change due to compression, so the ±5px tolerance is unnecessary — it could accept slightly wrong answers (e.g., 1420x2530). Setting tolerance=0 would be more precise, though this is a minor issue.
